stem: A hospital network must both continuously verify that every Amazon S3 bucket keeps default encryption enabled and ensure every bucket carries an approved DataClassification tag, across all of its AWS Organizations accounts. Which TWO controls together satisfy this? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: An AWS Config rule that evaluates each bucket's default encryption configuration on an ongoing basis
A one-time manual review of every bucket's settings during the next audit cycle
An AWS Organizations tag policy that defines the approved DataClassification values
An IAM permissions boundary that limits which S3 actions a role may take
A Glacier Vault Lock policy applied to each bucket

rationale: An AWS Config rule continuously evaluates whether each bucket's default encryption stays enabled, which is exactly the ongoing verification this scenario needs, and an AWS Organizations tag policy defines and enforces the approved DataClassification values across every account. A one-time manual review only captures a single point in time and does not continuously verify anything going forward. An IAM permissions boundary sets the maximum permissions a role can be granted; it does not evaluate resource configuration or tag values at all. Glacier Vault Lock is a WORM control for the legacy standalone Amazon Glacier vault service, not a control that can be applied to an S3 bucket.
